content: I'll split this bead into 4 smaller, focused child beads that build on each other sequentially.

args.command:
bead create --title "Locate CLI parsing entry point" \
  --description "## Scope
Find the entry point for CLI argument parsing in the codebase.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Located the main CLI entry file (likely src/main.rs or src/cli.rs)
- Identified the CLI framework being used (clap, argparse, etc.)
- Documented the file path in a note or comment

## Next Step
This enables finding the SearchOptions struct in the next bead." \
  --label split-child \
  --priority 2 \
  --issue-type task

bead create --title "Identify SearchOptions struct" \
  --description "## Scope
Find the specific struct that defines search command CLI options.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Located the SearchOptions or SearchCommand struct (or equivalent)
- Documented the exact file path and struct name
- Listed all current fields/flags in the struct
- Noted the struct's visibility (pub, internal, etc.)

## Dependencies
Requires knowing the CLI entry point from previous bead.

## Next Step
Understanding the struct enables analyzing flag patterns next." \
  --label split-child \
  --priority 2 \
  --issue-type task

bead create --title "Analyze existing flag patterns" \
  --description "## Scope
Document how existing CLI flags are implemented in the search command.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Documented the pattern used for flag definitions (clap::Parser attributes, field types, etc.)
- Identified 2-3 example flags and their implementation
- Noted any helper functions or macros used for flag parsing
- Documented how flags are passed from CLI to the search logic

## Dependencies
Requires having located the SearchOptions struct from previous bead.

## Next Step
This pattern understanding enables proper placement of the new --tag flag." \
  --label split-child \
  --priority 2 \
  --issue-type task

bead create --title "Add placement comment for --tag flag" \
  --description "## Scope
Add a clear code comment or note indicating where the --tag flag should be implemented.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Added a comment in the SearchOptions struct indicating --tag placement
- Comment includes example of the expected pattern based on existing flags
- If appropriate, added a TODO or FIXME marker
- Documented the flag type (e.g., Vec<String>, Option<String>)

## Dependencies
Requires understanding the flag patterns from previous bead.

## Next Step
This bead completes the documentation for implementing --tag later." \
  --label split-child \
  --priority 2 \
  --issue-type task
